## It Starts With
## **Healthy Roots**

[ Field Solutions][11]

Photo by Mel Machado

# AgBioChem, Inc., provides the most effective crown gall control products available.


Infected tree tumors (galls)


Pathogenic bacteria (Agrobacterium tumefaciens) attaching to plant wound

## The Problem

Crown gall is a plant “cancer” responsible for significant commercial losses in almond, walnut,
pecan, cherry, plum, prune, peach, nectarine, apricot, apple, pear, grape, caneberry, blueberry,
ornamentals (e.g., rose, euonymus, willow, poplar, etc.), and other plants.  Infected plants develop
expanding tumors (galls) that damage roots and trunks, resulting in weakened, less-productive plants
– and sometimes plant death.

**In almond trees, galls provide entry points for wood decay fungi that cause trees to “blow down”
(topple) during high winds.**

The crown gall pathogen is present in almost all soils and infects plants via fresh wounds created
during propagation, nursery digging, pre-plant handling, transplantation, and in-field mechanical
injury (e.g., grafting, pruning, cultivation).

### Disease Cycle

[Galltrol]

## The Solution

Growers have only ONE chance to prevent crown gall disease, and that is WTHIN 12 HOURS OF WOUNDING
and BEFORE trees, vines, and plants are planted.

Like all cancers – an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.

**Each plate of GALLTROL-A contains 120 BILLION freshly-grown, active bacterial cells that colonize
wounds and block infection.**

### **Galltroll-A®** prevents crown gall disease!
### **Gallex®** eradicates existing galls!

From industry leading post-harvest quality and freshness solutions to digital technology platforms
that answer your unique challenges, we’re 100% focused on what fresh means to you. As the pioneers
behind the introduction of 1-MCP for ethylene management, as well as Uvasys, the world’s first
laminated SO2 generating sheets product, we deliver answers at every step of the supply chain to
help your produce—and your business—get where it needs to go.

[Learn More][71]

## Answers from all angles.

We have leading near- and post-harvest products and services that answer real quality and freshness
challenges throughout the fresh produce supply chain.

Mating disruption uses pests’ own sexual communication signals to confuse them. These communication
signals are chemicals called pheromones, and they have no effect on any other species but the target
pest. With extra pheromone in the air, males can’t find females to mate. Less mating means less
offspring, and less offspring means less crop damage.

# Farmers for our future.

Farming has always been about feeding communities and nurturing the land. Today, this remains the
goal of millions of hard-working farmers worldwide. Technology is opening new horizons for them,
allowing them to produce more food with less resources, a vital goal in a planet with growing needs.
Our Farmer-First strategy is about understanding farmers’ pain points so we can better serve them. 

[ 2025 Annual Report ][84] [ 2025 Sustainability Suite ][85]
[Together, we’re helping change the world for good.]

## Legacies of the Land

A U.S. campaign honoring 250 years of farming heritage**
American farming families have shaped the land for generations.**

*Legacies of the Land* brings their stories forward — told in their own words, on the farms they
call home.

[ Watch the stories ][86]
[Fendt RoGator 600 Series]

## A proud portfolio of legendary brands.

AGCO's leading brands support farmers as they transform the agricultural industry. Our innovative
solutions and a Farmer-First mentality are changing the landscape for farmers across the world.

## Sowing the seeds of ingenuity.

AGCO's precision technologies are revolutionizing the way we farm the land. By harnessing the power

### AccelWater (H2020)

Accelerating Water Circularity in Food and Beverage Industrial Areas around Europe
The food and beverage industry is one of the most water- and energy-intensive industries in the
world in addition to producing large volumes of waste. Therefore, freshwater supplies are in high
demand. Despite significant progress in improving water use efficiency, the food and beverage sector
needs to do more to minimise the use of freshwater during the processing of raw materials. However,
current solutions for wastewater treatment in industries under a water–waste–energy nexus remain
limited. The aim of the EU-funded AccelWater project is to change this pattern and improve
freshwater consumption in the food and beverage industry by focusing on developing novel water
reclaiming and reusing as well as artificial intelligence-enabled monitoring and control
technologies.

[AccelWater (H2020)]

### AccelWater (H2020)

Accelerating Water Circularity in Food and Beverage Industrial Areas around Europe
The food and beverage industry is one of the most water- and energy-intensive industries in the
world in addition to producing large volumes of waste. Therefore, freshwater supplies are in high
demand. Despite significant progress in improving water use efficiency, the food and beverage sector
needs to do more to minimise the use of freshwater during the processing of raw materials. However,
current solutions for wastewater treatment in industries under a water–waste–energy nexus remain
limited. The aim of the EU-funded AccelWater project is to change this pattern and improve
freshwater consumption in the food and beverage industry by focusing on developing novel water
reclaiming and reusing as well as artificial intelligence-enabled monitoring and control
technologies.
[Hydrousa (H2020)]

### Hydrousa (H2020)

Demonstration of water loops with innovative regenerative business models for the Mediterranean
region
This project aims to revolutionise water value chains in Mediterranean areas and beyond, by
providing innovative nature-based water management solutions, which will close water loops and boost
the agricultural and energy profile of these areas. AGENSO is responsible for the development of:
* an online monitoring and controlling platform for water loops
* an automated system for optimizing irrigation at agricultural sites based on open source
  technologies
* a serious game for disseminating the project results
[OPTIMA (H2020)]

### OPTIMA (H2020)

Optimised Pest Integrated Management to precisely detect and control plant diseases in perennial
crops and open-field vegetables
OPTIMA will develop an environmentally friendly IPM framework for vineyards, apple orchards and
carrots by providing a holistic integrated approach which includes all critical aspects related to
integrated disease management, such as:
* novel bio-PPPs use
* disease prediction models
* spectral early disease detection systems
* precision spraying techniques
AGENSO is responsible for the development of an innovative DSS with optimized disease prediction
models, using agro-climatic and biological algorithms; users’ testimonies; and geostatistical
methods.

# Pest CONTROL Professionals of Indiana

Does your home or business have a pest issue? Call American Pest Professionals for prompt, effective
pest control in East Central Indiana. We’ll ensure that you don’t have to put up with unwanted
guests on your property.

[ Button ][38]

## Pest Control Services

At American Pest Professionals, we live up to our name by offering professional, high-quality
services that address our client’s specific needs. Whether you have an outbreak of bedbugs or
reoccurring rodent problems, you can count on us to provide specific pest management methods that
will address your problem.

We don’t believe in a one-size-fits-all approach to pest control. Our team understands that every
pest situation is unique, so we make a point to Inspect, Detect, and then Correct. We’ll inspect
your property, detect the exact nature of your pest issues, and craft a solution to correct the
problem.

We offer inspections and estimates for free because you deserve to know how extensive your pest
problem is and how we plan to treat it before you pay.

[Baxter Pest Professionals logo with a red outline of the US and blue and red text.]

### proud home of

### ﻿BAXTER PEST PROFESSIONALS!

## Pest Control Experience

American Pest Professionals has proudly served the communities of East Central Indiana since 1936.
Though the pests are the same, our methods have become even more effective and environmentally
friendly over decades of experience. We know what will work on Indiana pests, and we have the
resources and expertise to follow through on the best treatments.

If you need qualified, experienced pest control services in East Central Indiana, give American Pest
Professionals a call at [765-288-7779][39]

pest control in East Central Indiana. We’ll ensure that you don’t have to put up with unwanted
guests on your property.

[ Button ][38]

At American Pest Professionals, we live up to our name by offering professional, high-quality
services that address our client’s specific needs. Whether you have an outbreak of bedbugs or
reoccurring rodent problems, you can count on us to provide specific pest management methods that
will address your problem.

pest situation is unique, so we make a point to Inspect, Detect, and then Correct. We’ll inspect

problem.

## Social

## About ME

#### What is Buglady Consulting?

Buglady Consulting provides pest management consulting services to various sectors of the
horticulture industry. Specializing in biological control as part of an Integrated Pest Management
(IPM) program, all client recommendations aim to manage pests in a financially and ecologically
responsible manner. With 25 years in business, Buglady Consulting serves a diverse customer base,
including ornamentals, cannabis, vegetables, CEA systems, interiorscapes and theme parks. The
company is owned by Suzanne Wainwright-Evans.
* [Suzanne Wainwright-Evans][21] [Bio][22]
* [Photo Gallery][23]
* [Social Media ][24]

#### Services Provided

**Consulting**

Pulling from 30 years of industry experience, Suzanne provides expert advice on pest management and
plant health care, focusing on IPM. Recommendations are made using reduced risk products, biological
control agents, and other cultural practices. 



**Onsite Pest Management Training**

Provides hands on, in the field training on pests and biological control agents. This can be done
done for greenhouse,  nursery,  indoor grows, CEA systems and garden center employees.

 

**Lecturing**

Suzanne has spoken across the United States and internationally on a wide range of topics, including
insect identification, sustainable pest management, biological control, and beneficial insect
conservation. She also provides in-depth training on scouting. Her classes feature a vast collection
of macro photography images that she has captured over many decades

# Creating a *more*
# *food secure* world

Our planet’s population is growing rapidly — and so is the need for more food. Already, 800 million
people go to bed hungry each night. As a food company to the world, Cargill is partnering with
farmers and customers to grow and produce more food with less impact, to move that food to store
shelves and family tables, and to nourish people for a more food secure world.

[Watch the video][52]

**GROW**

### [Meet the farmers building our food-secure world][53]

**MOVE**

### [Advancing decarbonization across the food supply chain][54]

**NOURISH**

### [Discover how we’re building resilient food systems][55]

## 2025 Annual Report

#### Connecting a food secure world

The food you eat has a story to tell. Because before you take that first bite, a global network of
hard-working people – spanning countries, cultures and skillsets – each did their part to grow, make
and move your meal from where it was grown to the fork in your hand. At Cargill, it’s our privilege
to facilitate the complex connections that make it all happen.

In Cargill’s 2025 Annual Report, we share how we’re strengthening ties between farmers, frontline
food workers and the customers we exist to serve. Learn how our collective efforts are helping
transform food and agriculture and connect a food secure world.

[Read the Report][56]

[2025 annual report feature image]

 

 

[2025 Impact report feature image]

## 2025 Impact Report

#### Building a more resilient food system

As a company that sits at the center of the global food system, Cargill plays a unique role in
connecting farmers, food producers, and consumers. This vantage point makes it clear that the future
of food depends on a system that is productive, sustainable, and resilient.

In Cargill’s 2025 Impact Report, we share how our strategy reflects this interconnected view — how
growing food impacts natural resources; how it moves from where it’s grown; and how we partner to
expand access to nutrition, improve farmer and community livelihoods, and accelerate our customers’
progress on sustainability.

Together, we’re working to build a stronger, more sustainable food system that can nourish the world
for generations to come.

[Read the Report][57]

 

 

## Our purpose

#### To nourish the world in a safe, responsible and sustainable way

Sitting at the heart of the global supply chain, we join farmers, ranchers, manufacturers,
foodservice customers and retailers in sourcing, making and delivering products that are vital for
living.

Every day, our 155K+ team members come to work:
* Driven to improve lives through food, nutrition and health
* Looking for ways to innovate with purpose
* Committed to nourishing our growing world by providing access to life’s essentials

This is how we create new opportunities for our customers to grow, communities to prosper and
consumers to live well.

[Read about Cargill][58]

[Our purpose]

 

 

 

 

## People

 

With 155K+ colleagues in 70 countries, we work as a global network to bring together the people,
ideas and resources that can nourish lives around the world.

[Careers][59]

## Products

 

Partnering across the supply chain, we bring food, ingredients, agricultural solutions and
industrial products to meet customers’ ever-evolving needs.

[Products & Services][60]

## Planet

 

From small family farms to global shipping lanes, we work every day to bring new sustainable
practices, reduce our impact on the planet and take care of people.

[Sustainability][61]

What are others saying about our impact? With operations in 70 countries, Cargill and our customers
are making news around the globe. Here a

## Experts in Entomology

Insects are found in almost every inhabitable environment throughout the world. While they are
invaluable to their native ecosystems, they can also compromise the structural integrity of
buildings, sanctuary of homes and safety of food production. While every business needs pest control
services, pest consultants go a step further and face complex entomological issues while guiding
companies to solutions for pest-related problems. 

When addressing these pest-related issues, companies are safe with DOCS (Donny Oswalt Consulting
Services), an independent consulting firm specializing in urban and structural pest management
consulting.



DOCS is not a pest control company. Rather, the team of professionals at DOCS will assess the issue
and recommend best practices for mitigation or remediation of a wide range of entomological-related
issues. With over 30 years of experience providing solutions tailored to each client’s needs, DOCS
has the qualifications and expertise to address issues in the areas of:
* Litigation support 
* Tech assistance 
* Program evaluations
* On-site problem solving 
* Audit assistance 
* Training



﻿DOCS also specializes in the development and auditing of pest management programs for food handling,
healthcare, port authorities, commercial and government facilities.

[[A logo for donny oswalt consulting service]][11]

Our Story

Greentumble was founded in 2015 by Sara and Ovi with a mission to raise awareness about
environmental issues that affect us all.

We are an international couple living mainly in Europe. Sara comes originally from a small town in
Czech Republic and Ovi from a rural area in Romania.

We met in Austria when taking environmental science classes at the University of Natural Resources
and Life Sciences in Vienna. We fell in love and that’s how our great journey towards creating
Greentumble started.

From humble beginnings in 2015, we've grown into a platform that inspires readers to take action,
offering practical solutions for living sustainably. We believe that change starts with education.

As one global community, we need to keep learning about the environment around us and raise our
children to environmental empathy, because that is the only way to enjoy unlimited benefits of
nature.

Recruitment, onboarding, payroll, attendance, PMS, expense claims, exit, alumni — all under a single

Auto-computed PF, ESI, PT, LWF, and TDS across all 28 states. Statutory updates applied before you

Biometric, GPS, GeoMark+, or VISAGE face recognition — every punch flows into one leave and
attendance engine, straight through to payroll. No reconciliation spreadsheets.

Payslips, leave balances, claims, Form 16, tax declarations — employees access everything from the

## Welcome

Harmony Ecotech Pvt. Ltd. is an ISO 9001:2015 certified and Dun & Bradstreet registered company,
manufacturing & exporting a wide range of world class agri inputs, used by knowledgeable and
discerning farmers the world over in their "Integrated Pest Management (IPM) & Crop Health
Management" practices, by focussing on “Complete Customer Delight”.
Harmony Ecotech supplies its IPM products under the brand name ActiveIPM® and agri inputs such as
Bio-Fertilizers, Bio-pesticides, Growth Promoters, Probiotics / Microbial Cocktails etc. under the
brand name PRIDHVI and its Storage & Warehousing Pheromones & Traps under the brand name STORE
SAFE™.

## our Mission & vision

HARMONY ECOTECH endeavours to deliver optimum value to its customers through sustained emphasis on
innovative research to develop and deliver quality products at the most economical prices. Through
this proactive approach, the company hopes to contribute in its own small way to sustainable crop &
ecology management leading to a better balance between human life & nature.
For us at Harmony Ecotech, Nature is our Teacher!
By closely and continuously observing “Nature’s Ways”, combining time tested practices and
state-of-the-art technologies and adapting them to the current day needs, Harmony Ecotech develops,
produces and markets products such as Pheromone Lures and Insect Traps, Microbial Cocktails,
Bio-fertilizers, Plant Growth Promoters & Bio-stimulants, and Bio-Pesticides to protect crops from
pest attacks, disease incidence and promote crop health – be it of fruits, vegetables, flowers,
cereals or food grains.
[duns-iso]

### About Icon

We are the professional membership body for the conservation profession and a charity working to
safeguard cultural heritage

[Find Out More][277]

### [Find a conservator you can trust][278]

The most reliable way to identify and contact professional conservators to care for your objects and
collections

[Search the Directory][279]

### Current conservation and heritage science jobs

Check out the latest vacancies and opportunities

[Visit our jobs page][280]

### Exploring the Path to a Royal Charter

Find out what a Royal Chartership could mean for Icon, our members, and the future of the
conservation profession

[Learn More][281]

### The Icon Conference 2026: Practice, People, and Purpose

Shining a spotlight on the transformative power of the Conservation profession

[Find Out More][282]

#### Latest news

[ [HSE_YGT_130726_4.jpg] ][283]
20 Jul 2026

#### [ Advocacy in action: HSE & Icon visit York Glaziers Trust ][284]

On 13 July 2026, representatives from the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) visited York Glaziers
Trust as part of their ongoing review of responses to the consultation on proposed changes to
workplace lead exposure limits under the Control of Lead at Work Regulations (CLAW 2002).

[News][285]
[ [Screenshot 2026-07-08 093437.jpg] ][286]
17 Jul 2026

#### [ The Latest Issue of Iconnect Magazine is Now Available! ][287]

We're thrilled to share that Issue 15 of Iconnect Magazine is out.

[News][288]
[ [1000040561.jpg] ][289]
16 Jul 2026

#### [ Have Your Say: Two ISO Standards Open for Public Consultation ][290]

Two draft international standards are currently open for public consultation, providing an
opportunity for conservation professionals to help shape their development.

[News][291]
[ [RICHeS AF 1st Call- Website cover images (1).png] ][292]
15 Jul 2026

#### [ RICHeS Access Fund opens heritage science infrastructure to new users across the UK ][293]

Over £500,000 awarded to enable 43 organisations across the UK to investigate historic sites, reveal
new stories about museum collections, improve conservation techniques and tackle some of the biggest
challenges facing cultural heritage through the first Research Infrastructure for Conservation and
Heritage Science (RICHeS) Access Fund.

[News][294]
[ [Icon26 staff photo.jpg] ][295]
29 Jun 2026

#### [ Reflecting on the Icon Conference 2026: Practice, People, and Purpose ][296]

The Icon Conference 2026 brought together the conservation community in Edinburgh for two days of
inspiring talks, poster sessions, and collaboration under the theme Practice, People, and Purpose.

[News][297]
[ [microscope scientist heritage science.jpg] ][298]
24 Jun 2026

#### [ UK-wide Heritage and Conservation Science Workforce Survey Launched ][299]

The survey will generate vital evidence to strengthen skills, planning and long-term resilience
across the sector.

[News][300]

17 Jun 2026

#### [ Meet Our Exhibitors for the Icon Conference 2026 ][302]

Discover the organisations exhibiting at Icon26

### **IKARI Team featured on Channel News Asia sharing tips on How to check for bedbugs when you
### travel**

## – and avoid bringing them home.

Are you planning a trip abroad? If so, it’s important to be aware of a significant bed bug problem
in Korea. Although bed bugs are not new or fatal, they can be quite a nuisance. Recently, there has
been an outbreak of bed bugs in Korea, causing increased concerns.

The increasing reports of bed bug cases have fueled public anxiety. Park Ku-yeon, an official in
charge, reported over 13 confirmed cases and several dozen suspected ones nationwide. As a result,
the government launched a four-week campaign to prevent and disinfect dormitories, buses, trains,
and other public areas.

### **Protect yourself from COVID-19**

## Disinfection Service & Sanitisers

In light of recent developments due to the COVID-19 outbreak, such as the lockdown in our
neighbouring countries and spike of COVID-19 cases, IKARI will provide disinfection services and
select disinfectants. To protect and help you achieve a peace of mind, IKARI can disinfect your
workplace or home of 99.99% of all viruses and bacteria with our suite disinfection products and
services.

**We are among NEA's List of companies that can carry out disinfection works.**

#### Pest Control

IKARI Pest Control is the comprehensive eco-friendly premium pest control solution for your pest
problems. As a pest stop, we’ve got you covered from ants, cockroaches, flies, bed bugs, termites,
rodents, mosquitoes, booklice, ticks/fleas, bees to snakes.

[Learn More][35]

## Did you Know?

#### We do not just 'SPRAY AND PRAY'

[Integrated Pest Management][36](IPM) is a pest management process that emphasizes environmental
management through regular inspections, planning strategies and making decisions, treatments,
evaluation and re-evaluation, and inspection again. It is designed to minimize pesticide use and
‘spraying’

#### IKARI's Philosophy

Our philosophy is to take a human-safe and low-toxic approach in dealing with all pest problems. We
are pioneers in the implementation of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) and continue to stay true to
this approach.

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 795

[Laurel Wreath]

Crop Profile

### [Crop Profile][45]

Crop profiles are snapshots of crop production practices for agricultural commodities. Usually
produced on a state-by-state basis, crop profiles provide agricultural statistics for the crop;
information on regions within the state; an inventory of pests and strategies used for their
management (e.g., cultural practices, biological control, and pesticides); and lists of key
contacts, references, and online resources. Crop profiles are considered living documents, so as the
pest management situation changes, older crop profiles are revised and updated versions made
available.

[Crop Profile History][46]

[Crop Profile Guidelines][47]

[Crop Profile RFA][48]

[Apply for Crop Profile Grant][49]

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 126

[Laurel Wreath]

Element

### [Element][50]

IPM Guidelines (also known as IPM Checklists, Elements, Protocols, Definitions, and Standards) are
best management practices for specific crops, developed in cooperation primarily with growers,
university Extension specialists, and IPM consultants. These guidelines are used by various programs
to qualify or certify that a grower or IPM practitioner is using accepted IPM practices. IPM
Guidelines have been evaluated for their practicality and are often assigned points based on their
importance to IPM and the level of difficulty required to implement. While these guidelines
represent the best management options currently available, they evolve as new IPM technologies are
developed. To learn how guidelines are created, see the IPM Institute’s [Guide to IPM Elements and
Guidelines][51].

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 203

[Laurel Wreath]

Pest Management Strategic Plan

### [Pest Management Strategic Plan][52]

Pest Management Strategic Plans (PMSPs) address pest management needs and priorities for individual
commodities in a particular state or region. The plans take a pest-by-pest approach to identifying
the current management practices (chemical and nonchemical) and those under development.

PMSPs are developed by growers, commodity associations, land-grant university specialists, food
processors, crop consultants, and the EPA. Plans include priorities for research, regulatory
activity, and education/training programs needed for transition to alternative pest management
practices.

[PMSP Guidelines][53]

[PMSP Workshop Guidelines][54]

[PMSP Workshop FAQs][55]

[PMSP RFA][56]

[Apply for PMSP Grant][57]

 

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 1

[Laurel Wreath]

Pest-centric Management Strategic Plan

### [Pest-centric Management Strategic Plan][58]

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 6

[Laurel Wreath]

Priority

### [Priority][59]

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 17

[Laurel Wreath]

Timeline

### [Timeline][60]

Timelines give a general overview of crop production, worker activities, and key pests in crops. The
timeline is intended to describe the activities and their relationship to pesticide applications
which take place throughout the year to be used in worker risk assessments, and where risks of
concern are identified, in the assessment of pesticide benefits. The timing of events described may
vary due to such factors as the geography, climate, and weather. Pesticide use information is
current as of the last update.

Pest Management Strategic Plans (PMSPs) include Timelines, as well.

###### integrated pest management datasources

## We deliver IPM data

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 795

[Laurel Wreath]

Crop Profile

### [Crop Profile][45]

Crop profiles are snapshots of crop production practices for agricultural commodities. Usually
produced on a state-by-state basis, crop profiles provide agricultural statistics for the crop;
information on regions within the state; an inventory of pests and strategies used for their
management (e.g., cultural practices, biological control, and pesticides); and lists of key
contacts, references, and online resources. Crop profiles are considered living documents, so as the
pest management situation changes, older crop profiles are revised and updated versions made
available.

[Crop Profile History][46]

[Crop Profile Guidelines][47]

[Crop Profile RFA][48]

[Apply for Crop Profile Grant][49]

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 126

[Laurel Wreath]

Element

### [Element][50]

IPM Guidelines (also known as IPM Checklists, Elements, Protocols, Definitions, and Standards) are
best management practices for specific crops, developed in cooperation primarily with growers,
university Extension specialists, and IPM consultants. These guidelines are used by various programs
to qualify or certify that a grower or IPM practitioner is using accepted IPM practices. IPM
Guidelines have been evaluated for their practicality and are often assigned points based on their
importance to IPM and the level of difficulty required to implement. While these guidelines
represent the best management options currently available, they evolve as new IPM technologies are
developed. To learn how guidelines are created, see the IPM Institute’s [Guide to IPM Elements and
Guidelines][51].

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 203

[Laurel Wreath]

Pest Management Strategic Plan

### [Pest Management Strategic Plan][52]

Pest Management Strategic Plans (PMSPs) address pest management needs and priorities for individual
commodities in a particular state or region. The plans take a pest-by-pest approach to identifying
the current management practices (chemical and nonchemical) and those under development.

PMSPs are developed by growers, commodity associations, land-grant university specialists, food
processors, crop consultants, and the EPA. Plans include priorities for research, regulatory
activity, and education/training programs needed for transition to alternative pest management
practices.

[PMSP Guidelines][53]

[PMSP Workshop Guidelines][54]

[PMSP Workshop FAQs][55]

[PMSP RFA][56]

[Apply for PMSP Grant][57]

[Laurel Wreath]

[Laurel Wreath]

Priority

### [Priority][59]

[Laurel Wreath]

#### 17

[Laurel Wreath]

Timeline

### [Timeline][60]

Timelines give a general overview of crop production, worker activities, and key pests in crops. The
timeline is intended to describe the activities and their relationship to pesticide applications
which take place throughout the year to be used in worker risk assessments, and where risks of
concern are identified, in the assessment of pesticide benefits. The timing of events described may
vary due to such factors as the geography, climate, and weather. Pesticide use information is
current as of the last update.

Pest Management Strategic Plans (PMSPs) include Timelines, as well.

## Termite Control

J&J Exterminating offers some very effective weapons against termite infestation of your home and/or
business. The Termidor® System places a treated zone in the soil around your home, while the
[Sentricon® System][52] makes use of monitoring/baiting stations directly in the ground around your
home. Both systems are effective in preventing termite infestation as well as controlling existing
colonies. Your technician will work with you to determine the best protection for you.

## Residential Pest Control

Gold Shield 365 makes protecting your home easy and convenient. Gold Shield 365 uses the effective
techniques of Integrated Pest Management, which means fewer products and more exclusion, keeping
pests out of your home with proven, long-lasting baits and blocking their entry with physical and
residual barriers.

## Commercial Pest Control

J&J Exterminating offers pest control services to Banks, Hospitals, Food Services, Food Processing,
Food & Non-Food Retailers, Office Buildings, Hospitality Industries, Health Care, Manufacturing, and
Warehouse Food Distribution. J&J Exterminating products are AIB Certified as well as USDA
Governmental FDA Regulated.

## Rodent Control

Rodents can be a major issue in any commercial setting, costing lost revenue and customers. They
serve as vectors for disease as they are able to carry bacteria in their systems and transmit it
elsewhere. Rodents are generally nocturnal and daytime sightings could represent a large
population.  Through exclusion methods, baiting and trapping, we can handle any size establishment
and any issue that arises.

## Bed Bug Treatment

They live everywhere, not just in your mattress. Bed bugs can hide in furniture and behind wall
cove

## Termite Control

J&J Exterminating offers some very effective weapons against termite infestation of your home and/or
business. The Termidor® System places a treated zone in the soil around your home, while the
[Sentricon® System][52] makes use of monitoring/baiting stations directly in the ground around your
home. Both systems are effective in preventing termite infestation as well as controlling existing
colonies. Your technician will work with you to determine the best protection for you.

## Residential Pest Control

Gold Shield 365 makes protecting your home easy and convenient. Gold Shield 365 uses the effective
techniques of Integrated Pest Management, which means fewer products and more exclusion, keeping
pests out of your home with proven, long-lasting baits and blocking their entry with physical and
residual barriers.

## Commercial Pest Control

J&J Exterminating offers pest control services to Banks, Hospitals, Food Services, Food Processing,
Food & Non-Food Retailers, Office Buildings, Hospitality Industries, Health Care, Manufacturing, and
Warehouse Food Distribution. J&J Exterminating products are AIB Certified as well as USDA
Governmental FDA Regulated.

## Rodent Control

Rodents can be a major issue in any commercial setting, costing lost revenue and customers. They
serve as vectors for disease as they are able to carry bacteria in their systems and transmit it
elsewhere. Rodents are generally nocturnal and daytime sightings could represent a large
population.  Through exclusion methods, baiting and trapping, we can handle any size establishment
and any issue that arises.

## Bed Bug Treatment

They live everywhere, not just in your mattress. Bed bugs can hide in furniture and behind wall
coverings…and you are on the menu. Getting rid of bed bugs is not an easy process. Bed bug
infestation will require treatment by a pest control experts. We at J&J Exterminating are extremely
concerned with the latest news reports concerning the spread of bed bugs. The insects are spreading
quickly through luggage, hand bags, and purses.

## Who We Are

Kubota uses a wide range of products and technologies to provide solutions in the areas of food,
water, and the environment, which are indispensable for people's lives. From a grain of rice or a
drop of water to the foundations of society and industry, Kubota's solutions support the lives of
human beings.
* ### [Agriculture][170]
  
  As a comprehensive solutions provider for agriculture, Kubota offers total support at every stage
  of farming, from developing agricultural machinery that meets farmers' needs to the production,
  processing and consumption of agricultural products. Kubota supports farming throughout the world
  and contributes to a more prosperous future for people and food.
  
  [
  ][171]
* ### [Water][172]
  
  Kubota's water environment solutions are active in all aspects of the water cycle, supporting
  water infrastructure in Japan and throughout the world. As a water treatment specialist, we are
  committed to finding solutions to the world's water problems and supplying safe water to all
  people in the world.
  
  [
  ][173]
* ### [Environment][174]
  
  Social infrastructure is indispensable for our prosperous and comfortable lives. Industrial
  infrastructure serves as the foundation for manufacturing. Kubota answers the needs of society to
  offer solutions that support these infrastructures, contributing to more affluent lives for
  humans.
  
  [
  ][175]

[Groundwork for Tomorrow][176]

## Innovation

Kubota envisions the social issues that could arise in the near future and creates new services and
business and develops products in anticipation if these issues, contributing even further to
society.

[Learn More][177]

## Sustainability

Kubota considers food, water and the environment as a singular theme, and aims to realize a
sustainable society through a proper cycle of these elements using technology and solutions.

[Learn More][178]

## Who We Are

Kubota uses a wide range of products and technologies to provide solutions in the areas of food,
water, and the environment, which are indispensable for people's lives. From a grain of rice or a
drop of water to the foundations of society and industry, Kubota's solutions support the lives of
human beings.
* ### [Agriculture][170]
  
  As a comprehensive solutions provider for agriculture, Kubota offers total support at every stage
  of farming, from developing agricultural machinery that meets farmers' needs to the production,
  processing and consumption of agricultural products. Kubota supports farming throughout the world
  and contributes to a more prosperous future for people and food.
  
  [
  ][171]
* ### [Water][172]
  
  Kubota's water environment solutions are active in all aspects of the water cycle, supporting
  water infrastructure in Japan and throughout the world. As a water treatment specialist, we are
  committed to finding solutions to the world's water problems and supplying safe water to all
  people in the world.
  
  [
  ][173]
* ### [Environment][174]
  
  Social infrastructure is indispensable for our prosperous and comfortable lives. Industrial
  infrastructure serves as the foundation for manufacturing. Kubota answers the needs of society to
  offer solutions that support these infrastructures, contributing to more affluent lives for
  humans.
  
  [
  ][175]

[Groundwork for Tomorrow][176]

## Innovation

Kubota envisions the social issues that could arise in the near future and creates new services and
business and develops products in anticipation if these issues, contributing even further to
society.

[Learn More][177]

## Sustainability

Kubota considers food, water and the environment as a singular theme, and aims to realize a
sustainable society through a proper cycle of these elements using technology and solutions.

innovative products, years of experience and strategic recommendations to every pest challenge. No

## [ABOUT US][30]

**N**olan **I**ntegrated **P**est **C**ontrol **A**nd **M**anagement (NIPCAM) Group is just that, a
group of companies that each provide a unique and specialized pest related service.  Our services
include: [pest management consulting][31], [termite litigation][32], [pest management service
work][33], [pest control product sales][34] and [testing/development][35].  You have pests?  NIPCAM
Group provides pest solutions.

[

## 50 + YEARS of EXPERIENCE

][36]

NIPCAM offers an unparalleled level of experience and expertise in the pest management field.  Our
PhD team members helped found many of the integrated pest management (IPM) practices used in the
industry today.  When you have a problem that needs critical attention, you can be assured that our
team is up to the challenge.

# Protecting public health, food, and property

NPMA proudly serves over 4,000 member companies and their employees in the pest management
community. We do that through education, industry leadership, public policy initiatives, and market
development resources.

## Upcoming Events
* [ **July 28, 2026 | 2:00 PM EDT**

  The SPAR Summer Series sessions focus on skills for our State Policy Affairs Representatives
  (SPARs) and any interested members to enhance their advocacy efforts.
  
  ][164]

  Attend diverse educational opportunities, including comprehensive management sessions, engaging
  training sessions, and cutting-edge technical courses highlighting the latest advancements in pest
  management, while attending family-friendly social functions.
  
  ][165]

[ [Abamectin 5% EC] ][54]
[Abamectin 5% EC][55]
[Abamectin 5% EC is a potent insecticide, acaricide, and nematicide formulated as an emulsifiable
concentrate. Derived from Streptomyces avermitilis, it offers contact and stomach activity with
limited systemic movement and translaminar action. Effective against mites, aphids, thrips,
leafminers, and nematodes, it's suitable for various crops, including vegetables, fruit trees, and
ornamentals.][56]
[ [Abamectin 1.8% EC] ][57]
[Abamectin 1.8% EC][58]
[Abamectin 1.8% EC is a potent macrocyclic lactone insecticide/acaricide that acts rapidly through
contact and ingestion, disrupting the nervous system of pests. It binds to glutamate- and GABA-gated
chloride channels, causing hyperpolarization, paralysis, and death, with translaminar penetration
reaching concealed pests like mites and leafminers.][59]
[ [30% Chlorfenapyr·Indoxacarb SC] ][60]
[Chlorfenapy15%r·Indoxacarb15% SC][61]
[Chlorfenapyr15% + Indoxacarb 15% SC is a dual-action suspension concentrate that delivers powerful,
broad-spectrum pest control by combining two distinct modes of action. This combination ensures
immediate knockdown and sustained protection, making it an effective rotation partner in integrated
pest management programs.][62]

workshop on stored product pests. The workshop, which takes place Sept. 15-16, is open to all
interested individuals.

## World leading supplier of pest control products for professional and retail markets

#### The Pelsis Academy

The Pelsis Academy is the leading pest control training facility at the Pelsis Group's headquarters
in North Yorkshire. The Pelsis Academy benefits from three state of the art training rooms as well
as a two-storey pest training house making it the perfect place to learn all aspects of pest
control.

The Pelsis Academy is designed to provide pest controllers with a vibrant environment to develop
their pest control knowledge and skills. The training facility offers the chance to create scenarios
so you can hone your pest control skills and application methods in an environment that replicates
real life scenarios.

The Pelsis Academy is the leading pest control training facility at the Pelsis Group's headquarters
in North Yorkshire. The Pelsis Academy benefits from three state of the art training rooms as well
as a two-storey pest training house making it the perfect place to learn all aspects of pest
control.

The Pelsis Academy is designed to provide pest controllers with a vibrant environment to develop
their pest control knowledge and skills. The training facility offers the chance to create scenarios
so you can hone your pest control skills and application methods in an environment that replicates
real life scenarios.

## Nos produits d’alerte pour un contrôle
## ciblé, économique et écologique

### Votre partenaire depuis
### 35 ans pour lutter contre les ravageurs de vos cultures

Chez Bioprox Phéromones, nous vendons des phéromones conçues par l’INRAe ainsi que des pièges et
l’ensemble du matériel nécessaire à la surveillance et au contrôle des insectes ravageurs pour
toutes les productions végétales en agriculture. Forts de plus de 35 ans d’expertise, nous
fournissons des solutions d’alerte fiables, économiques et respectueuses de l’environnement pour
toutes les cultures végétales.

### Les phéromones en agriculture : un moyen d’alerte écologique

Les phéromones représentent une solution efficace pour la gestion des ravageurs en agriculture.
Inspirées du biomimétisme, les phéromones imitent les signaux sexuels émis naturellement par les
insectes pour perturber leur reproduction ou détecter leur présence. Spécifiques à chaque ravageur,
elles permettent une gestion ciblée sans répercussions négatives sur les auxiliaires, ni la
biodiversité.

### Le piégeage par phéromones, un outil d'aide à la décision

Par les captures des mâles, ce piégeage sexuel par phéromones fournit des informations précieuses
pour une lutte contre les insectes ravageurs plus facile, mieux ciblée et plus économique pour
l’agriculteur.

#### PRÉVENTION

Une bonne détection des insectes ravageurs pour un inventaire précis d’espèces à combattre

#### MONITORING

Le degré d’intensification de la population sur une période de temps donnée

#### PRÉCISION

Traitement localisé et époque d’application du produit optimisée

#### ÉVALUATION

Une idée précise de la répartition à l’échelle d’une culture donnée

Pour optimiser l’efficacité de nos pièges et phéromones de monitoring, pensez à croiser leur
utilisation avec les données issues du Bulletin de santé du végétal (BSV). Ce bulletin régional, mis
à jour régulièrement, vous indique le moment idéal pour l’installation ou le remplacement des
dispositifs, en fonction du stade de développement des ravageurs observés sur le terrain et de leurs
pics de vol.

### Les phéromones en agriculture : un moyen d’alerte écologique

Les phéromones représentent une solution efficace pour la gestion des ravageurs en agriculture.
Inspirées du biomimétisme, les phéromones imitent les signaux sexuels émis naturellement par les
insectes pour perturber leur reproduction ou détecter leur présence. Spécifiques à chaque ravageur,
elles permettent une gestion ciblée sans répercussions négatives sur les auxiliaires, ni la
biodiversité.

# Inspired by Nature Powered by Science

## Harnessing Insect Pheromones for Sustainable Crop Management

[ Learn more ][25]

## Welcome to PheroSyn
## Leading the Natural Farming Revolution

PheroSyn is a supplier of pheromone-based insect monitoring and control solutions.

By utilising nature’s own chemical signals, we mimic insect communication to create targeted
products with remarkable specificity — helping protect non-target species and preserve
biodiversity. 

By combining cutting-edge research with real-world expertise, we empower farmers to achieve
sustainable, resilient harvests while fostering ecological balance.

Together, we’re building a future where agriculture thrives in harmony with nature.

Innovative Sustainable Partnership Research

### Innovative Solutions,
### Real-World Impact

Using pheromone-based technologies, we work to empower growers with tools that are effective and
sustainable. By targeting specific insect behaviours, our solutions reduce the need for conventional
pesticides, offering precision management while minimising harm to beneficial organisms.

Our commitment to innovation ensures farmers can adapt to environmental changes and market demands.

[pea leaf weevil pic]

### Sustainability at the Core

Sustainability is not just a principle—it’s our purpose. Every product we create and every solution
we offer aims to reduce environmental impact while maintaining high levels of agricultural
productivity.

We strive to provide farmers with new tools to manage insects without disrupting biodiversity. This
approach not only benefits the environment but also supports growers in meeting market and
regulatory demands for more sustainable practices. We try to make every action contribute to a
greener, more resilient planet for future generations.

[Bee pic]

### A Partnership Approach

Collaboration drives success, and PheroSyn takes pride in forming meaningful partnerships with
farmers, researchers, and industry leaders. Together, we innovate solutions that address both
current and future agricultural challenges.

Through workshops, field trials, and shared insights, we bridge the gap between science and
practical application. By listening to our partners and acting on their needs, we co-create
strategies that foster sustainability and long-term profitability, ensuring our solutions are as
effective in the field as they are in theory.

[Daniel et al New IPM pic]

### Driving Innovation Through Research

Innovation starts with inquiry, and at PheroSyn, we continuously push boundaries in research and
development. Our dedicated team works tirelessly to understand pest behaviours, crop ecosystems, and
the complex dynamics of modern agriculture.

By leveraging this knowledge, we create cutting-edge pheromone solutions that tackle the root causes
of pest challenges. Our commitment to innovation ensures that farmers always have access to
state-of-the-art tools that evolve alongside their needs, supporting a dynamic and resilient
agricultural industry.

[Daniel in lab 1]

## Precision Pheromone Solutions:
## Redefining Sustainable Pest Control

Empower your farming with precise pheromone solutions that effectively target pest behaviours,
reduce reliance on harmful chemical pesticides, and protect the health of your crops. Our field
trials, using monitoring technologies alone, have demonstrated up to 100% reduction in the use of
pesticides and a 40% increase in yields (data from pea trials in the UK). 

Our innovative technologies are designed to promote sustainable farming practices, preserve
biodiversity, and support the growing need for environmentally responsible agriculture—delivering
reliable, long-term benefits for farmers and the planet alike. 

[peas pest control]

PheroSyn’s pheromone solutions for pea midge are designed to offer early detection and precise
control, protecting your crops from infestations. By minimising pesticide use, our products help

chemical pesticides.

## Our Vision for a More Sustainable Future

At PheroSyn, we utilise “Green Chemistry” techniques to develop and sell sustainable,
pheromone-based solutions that aim to reduce pesticide use and promote healthier crops. By combining
precision technology with environmental stewardship, we empower farmers to increase yields, enhance
biodiversity, and build a greener future for agriculture.

## PheroSyn’s Values

[Bug white]

### Act with Integrity & Honesty

Being realistic and honest with our customers, stakeholders and advisors enables us to reflect and
consider how our products and advice can influence sustainable farming well into the future. We
listen to our customers, and focus on high quality products that deliver value to our customers.

[Bug white]

### Foster our Corporate Culture

We strive for excellence through learning, enabling us to see opportunities for growth and be
transparent about our strengths and weaknesses. We provide training opportunities for our team and
seek feedback to encourage personal growth of individuals and the wider company. We embrace
diversity, are mindful of people’s backgrounds and experiences, actively seeking out diversity in
age, culture, gender, ethnicity, family and life experiences. Everyone at PheroSyn has an equal
chance to contribute to our success.

[Bug white]

### Focus on Sustainability

With sustainability at our core, we lead the start-up chemical space by adhering to and improving
practices such as the principles of Green Chemistry, being attuned to our energy footprints and ESG
practices. We seek the same of our suppliers – asking about their sustainability credentials and
values. We look to minimise our lab waste.

[Bug white]

### Attend to Family and Health

Peace at home and good health are so critical to getting the best from our people, and we seek to
make work and life act in synergy to avoid these worlds colliding. We actively seek out best
practices to keep our staff happy and healthy, allowing us to fulfil our vision as a company while
bringing everyone along on the journey.

## Leading the Natural Farming Revolution

PheroSyn is a supplier of pheromone-based insect monitoring and control solutions.

products with remarkable specificity — helping protect non-target species and preserve
biodiversity. 

By combining cutting-edge research with real-world expertise, we empower farmers to achieve
sustainable, resilient harvests while fostering ecological balance.

Together, we’re building a future where agriculture thrives in harmony with nature.

Innovative Sustainable Partnership Research

### Real-World Impact

Using pheromone-based technologies, we work to empower growers with tools that are effective and
sustainable. By targeting specific insect behaviours, our solutions reduce the need for conventional
pesticides, offering precision management while minimising harm to beneficial organisms.

Our commitment to innovation ensures farmers can adapt to environmental changes and market demands.

Sustainability is not just a principle—it’s our purpose. Every product we create and every solution
we offer aims to reduce environmental impact while maintaining high levels of agricultural
productivity.

approach not only benefits the environment but also supports growers in meeting market and
regulatory demands for more sustainable practices. We try to make every action contribute to a
greener, more resilient planet for future generations.

[Bee pic]

Collaboration drives success, and PheroSyn takes pride in forming meaningful partnerships with
farmers, researchers, and industry leaders. Together, we innovate solutions that address both
current and future agricultural challenges.

Through workshops, field trials, and shared insights, we bridge the gap between science and
practical application. By listening to our partners and acting on their needs, we co-create
strategies that foster sustainability and long-term profitability, ensuring our solutions are as
effective in the field as they are in theory.

[Daniel et al New IPM pic]

Innovation starts with inquiry, and at PheroSyn, we continuously push boundaries in research and
development. Our dedicated team works tirelessly to understand pest behaviours, crop ecosystems, and
the complex dynamics of modern agriculture.

By leveraging this knowledge, we create cutting-edge pheromone solutions that tackle the root causes
of pest challenges. Our commitment to innovation ensures that farmers always have access to
state-of-the-art tools that evolve alongside their needs, supporting a dynamic and resilient
agricultural industry.

[Daniel in lab 1]

## Our Vision for a More Sustainable Future

biodiversity, and build a greener future for agriculture.

## PheroSyn’s Values

[Bug white]

### Act with Integrity & Honesty

consider how our products and advice can influence sustainable farming well into the future. We
listen to our customers, and focus on high quality products that deliver value to our customers.

[Bug white]

### Foster our Corporate Culture

We strive for excellence through learning, enabling us to see opportunities for growth and be
transparent about our strengths and weaknesses. We provide training opportunities for our team and
seek feedback to encourage personal growth of individuals and the wider company. We embrace
diversity, are mindful of people’s backgrounds and experiences, actively seeking out diversity in
age, culture, gender, ethnicity, family and life experiences. Everyone at PheroSyn has an equal
chance to contribute to our success.

[Bug white]

### Focus on Sustainability

With sustainability at our core, we lead the start-up chemical space by adhering to and improving
practices such as the principles of Green Chemistry, being attuned to our energy footprints and ESG
practices. We seek the same of our suppliers – asking about their sustainability credentials and
values. We look to minimise our lab waste.

[Bug white]

Peace at home and good health are so critical to getting the best from our people, and we seek to
make work and life act in synergy to avoid these worlds colliding. We actively seek out best
practices to keep our staff happy and healthy, allowing us to fulfil our vision as a company while

## About Paul J. Bello ACE, BCE, MBA

[A man wearing mask]

#### Welcome

 Paul J. Bello is an award-winning expert in the pest management industry. He holds two prestigious
entomology certifications ; the ACE (Associate Certified Entomologist) and the BCE (Board Certified
Entomologist). He was Committee Member of the Year of the Florida Pest Management Association, named
Pace Setter Award recipient at Zeneca Professional Products and received CPCO's 2018 winner of the
Award of Excellence. 

Paul's knowledge and dedication to the industry has helped in every aspect of the pest industry;
advising with pest control associations, coaching pest control companies nationwide, and mentoring
PMP (Pest Management Professionals) to help them achieve their  potential. He also assists qualified
pest professionals to study for, take and pass their ACE and BCE exams to attain their professional
credentials.

[ LEARN MORE ABOUT PAUL][61]

#### The PJB Business Development Workshop

 In October 2025 Paul will host the eighteenth PJB Business Development Workshop at Pensacola Beach.
These Workshops have served to help pest professionals from across the country improve the financial
performance and service delivery of their business. In the photo on the right we see **Dr. Austin M.
Frishman** who joined us on our **PJB Workshop Cruise** on board Utopia of the Seas where we had a
great time together. Go to the **Events page** to learn more, **Register **and make room
**Reservations **to attend.

[View upcoming and previous events][62]
[A man taking pictures]

#### Education & Training

PJB Pest Management Consulting provides a variety of training sessions to fit the need of every pest
management professional and their business organizations. Training classes include:

Continuing Education

ACE/BCE Certification Effective Study

State Exam Prep Courses

Technical & Educational Courses

Technical Training

Staff Training

Technician Training

Office Staff

Business Development Workshops

Custom Training upon request

[More Info][63]

## CPCO's 2018 Award of Excellence

#### CPCO's 2018 Award of Excellence


At the **2018 CPCO Annual Fall Conference** at Macon, GA, the first **Wayne Weber Memorial Award of
Excellence** was presented to **Paul Bello**. During the presentation, it was noted how Paul, has
donated much of his time to help CPCO and its membership succeed these many years. In fact, he had
been an advisor to the association’s Board during the formative meetings and since its inception
during the 1990s. Over the years he generously conducted continuing education classes for members,
helped develop specialized seminars, created cooperative efforts with other organizations,
including P.E.S.T. Relief International, and provided numerous training classes at locations across
the State for the benefit of CPCO Association members. At the presentation of this award were his
wife **Mary Ann Bello** and his Pest Control Technology college professor **Dr. Austin M.
Frishman**.

## Have Questions?

## We’ve Got You Covered.

Can I spray while the predators are in the room?
We often treat sprays as knockdowns. Utilizing prior to release, our typical time frame looks like
spray Monday, release on Thursday and let the bugs do their job for 2-3 weeks depending upon the
program. Please confirm which spray you are using for specific reapplication time frame.
Will these bugs clean up an infestation?
Predators are not designed to clean infestations and should be introduced preventatively. However
they can still be utilized in specific situations, specifically for fungus gnats and spider mite
control. These approaches often combine several drenches and or foliar sprays prior to releasing
predators to ensure the population of pest is reduced to a manageable degree.
Does regular defoliation remove the good bugs?
Ultimately, yes there will be some bugs removed during defoliations, but it is negligible when we
consider the quantities we are introducing. We do try to time it up properly so that defoliations
occur just prior to release. Keeping on a recurring program schedule will ensure you always have
active bugs in the areas most needed.
When do you ship the bugs out after I place my order?

We have two shipment windows:

– Monday ordering for Friday delivery

**OR**

– Tuesday -Friday ordering for delivery the following week on Thursday

## We’ve Got You Covered.

Can I spray while the predators are in the room?
We often treat sprays as knockdowns. Utilizing prior to release, our typical time frame looks like
spray Monday, release on Thursday and let the bugs do their job for 2-3 weeks depending upon the
program. Please confirm which spray you are using for specific reapplication time frame.
Will these bugs clean up an infestation?
Predators are not designed to clean infestations and should be introduced preventatively. However
they can still be utilized in specific situations, specifically for fungus gnats and spider mite
control. These approaches often combine several drenches and or foliar sprays prior to releasing
predators to ensure the population of pest is reduced to a manageable degree.
Does regular defoliation remove the good bugs?
Ultimately, yes there will be some bugs removed during defoliations, but it is negligible when we
consider the quantities we are introducing. We do try to time it up properly so that defoliations
occur just prior to release. Keeping on a recurring program schedule will ensure you always have
active bugs in the areas most needed.
When do you ship the bugs out after I place my order?

We have two shipment windows:

– Monday ordering for Friday delivery

**OR**

– Tuesday -Friday ordering for delivery the following week on Thursday

## ** On-Demand Entomological & Pest Management Support**

Whether you are looking for a presenter for a meeting, pest identification and support, solutions
for tough pest problems, a site inspection, or an on-call virtual technical director, we have the
expertise to help.

## **Classroom Resources and Lessons**

We're currently working on lessons and other resources to help support K-12 teachers bring insects
into the classroom. In the meantime, get in touch if you want to discuss your plans on using insects
in your classroom.
* ##### Board Certified Entomologist
  
  Expertise in entomology and pest management that you can trust. Our founder, Ted Snyder, is a
  Board Certified Entomologist and has a Master's Degree in Entomology.
* ##### Award Winning E-Learning
  
  We take pride in using our extensive experience in pest management to provide practical
  information on pests that can be used in the field to solve challenging pest accounts, to learn
  new skills, and to expand your service offerings.
* ##### Industry Experience
  
  With 30 years experience in commercial and residential pest management, we understand the pest
  management industry because we come from the pest management industry.

### Pest Identification and Analysis

Solving the toughest pest problems requires proper identification. We can help get you the right
identification, find out if the sample is a pest species or not, and understand the essential facts
needed to control the pest. We can work with either photos or physical samples.

We are located in the greater Milwaukee metropolitan area. Contact us to drop off a specimen or to
arrange a house call or inspection.

### Account Troubleshooting and Site Inspections

Pest problems can be difficult to solve. We have the experience and expertise to help. Through
traveling to your site or examining images of your site, we can help determine why pests are present
and put together a plan of action to control the problem.

### In-Person Training and Project Support

We provide presentations at meetings and industry events,  quality assurance, IPM program review,
training program development, and other entomological support. We can provide you with the expertise
you need, when you need it.


### Editors and Publishers

#### Professional, reliable content on entomology and pest management for your readers, when you
#### need it.  We have publications in:
* Cabin Life Magazine
* Executive Housekeeping Today
* Food Safety Magazine
* Pest Control Technology Magazine
* Pest Control Magazine
* NPMA Commercial e-Newsletter
* Kansas Pest Control Association Newsletter

[Contact us today to discuss your writing or editorial project.][9]

### Pest Management Companies

#### Don't let technical errors appear in print!

With our experience in writing and editing company newsletters, marketing materials, and websites,
we can ensure that your text always appears professional and technically accurate.  [Contact us to
get started.][10]

#### Recent Publications:

[Food-Safety2013][PCT Apr 2005][CBN150501]


### We've Been in Your Shoes.  Or Boots.


We understand the pest management industry because we come from the pest management industry. 

Our founder, Ted Snyder, is a Board Certified Entomologist and has a Master's Degree in Entomology,
but rather than just learning about pest control from books and classes, he's worked as a
technician.  As a salesperson.  As a supervisor.  And as a technical director for a large regional
pest management company.  He still remembers the smell of Safrotin.

### International Experience... With Midwestern Hospitality

We've worked in four countries on two continents, but we haven't forgotten our roots and still love
getting hands on with technicians.

We have extensive experience setting up, supporting, and troubleshooting integrated pest management
programs at food service accounts, audited food processing facilities, and in pharmaceutical
environments. And we operate out of Wisconsin, where you can find the friendliest people in the US,
don't you know.

### Award-Winning Training

Anybody can read a PowerPoint slide filled with useless knowledge on pests.

We take pride in using our extensive experience in the theory and practice of pest management to
provide practical information on pests that can be used in the field to solve challenging pest
accounts, to learn new skills, and to expand your service offerings.

And we're not the only ones who say this - the Board Certified Entomologists of Mid-America awarded
one of our training programs with the Educational Project Award.  We can give you the training you
want and need - or review your existing training program and make recommendations for improvement.

A [SiteOrigin][11] Theme

Reinventing The Pest Management Industry Through Best-In-Class Service Providers


Who we are
Building a partnership of leading, contemporary pest management providers to establish a new
standard of service and care in the industry.

Precision Pest Partners was formed to provide a completely new alternative in the industry – we are
not your standard industry consolidator.

We are focused on bringing together the best and brightest in the industry to build enduring value
to our operating partners through delivering exceptional service to our customers and long-term
career opportunities to their employees.

[logo top.png]
The PPP Philosophy
Precision Pest Partners is an innovative pest management solution provider, utilizing contemporary
digital tools and technologies, in conjunction with highly skilled and trained employees, to enhance
the efficacy and efficiency of the treatment process.

# Biological crop solutions

## INTRODUCING 2 NEW INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY PLATFORMS

ProFarm discovers and produces naturally-derived technology platforms that offer reliable and
consistent efficacy.

**RINO**Tec™ Technology emerges as a novel and innovative new technology for the management of
insects, mites, and nematodes. Discovered and developed by ProFarm scientists, **RINO**Tec™
Technology refers to the organism, whole fermentation solution, processes, patents, and trade
secrets.

[Powered by RinoTec Technology logo]

UBP™ Technology, manufactured by ProFarm, is a proprietary organic molecular substrate comprised of
16 vital and essential macro and micro-nutrients that are bound in a complex carbon-based process.

The scientifically proven, patented nutrient technology enhances conditions for nutrient uptake,
resulting in a plant that can manage abiotic stress, such as herbicide damage and drought. The
result is a crop empowered to produce greater yield and improved quality.

[UBP™ Technology wordmark — Pro Farm precision agriculture platform]

## Explore the Largest Portfolio of Biological Technologies

Sustainable Choices without Sacrificing Agronomic Excellence

[ [Close up image of a boom sprayer with jets of spray directed towards a crop.] ][32]

[ [Crop nutrition and soil health supported by Pro Farm biological inputs] ][34]

## [Crop nutrition][35]

[ [Healthy crop field representing Pro Farm biological crop protection solutions] ][36]

## [Crop health][37]

[ See all products ][38]

## Farmer-focused Programs

Our products are made to easily incorporate into your existing operations and tank mix well with
many common crop inputs.

### An IPM Program for Conventional Acres
* Add biologicals to a conventional tank mix for improved efficacy.
* Rotate biologicals with conventional inputs to incorporate multiple modes of action and reduce
  chances of resistance.
* Utilize biologicals right before harvest to ensure the best crop quality without harvest or export
  restrictions.

## People you can trust

ProFarm is comprised of a global team with a deep passion for science, sustainability, and crop
performance. We are on a relentless pursuit to create a more sustainable planet through agriculture.

High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development
The High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development (HLPF) is the central United Nations
platform for the follow-up and review of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and its 17
Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The 2026 HLPF will be convened from Tuesday, 7 July, to

Science, Technology and Innovation
Science, technology and innovation (STI) are essential for advancing the SDGs, enabling
evidence-based decision-making, accelerating implementation, and scaling solutions to complex global
challenges. On 6-7 May 2026, the eleventh annual Multi-Stakeholder Forum on Science, Technology and
Innovation for the SDGs (STI Forum) will take place at United Nations Headquarters in New York.
[2026 STI Forum][74] [2026 STI Solutions Book][75] [Technology Facilitation Mechanism][76]
Global Sustainable Development Report
The Global Sustainable Development Report (GSDR) is a United Nations publication aiming to
strengthen the science-policy interface, produced once every four years to inform the quadrennial
SDG review deliberations. The next report is scheduled for release in September 2027 ahead of the
High-level Political Forum on sustainable development to be held under the auspices of the General
Assembly (SDG Summit). [Global Sustainable Development Report][77] [GSDR in 2027][78] [GSDR in
2023][79]
Energy
Achieving SDG7 will open a new world of opportunities for millions of people through new economic
opportunities and jobs, empowered women, children and youth, better education and health, more
sustainable, equitable and inclusive communities, and greater protections from, and resilience to,
climate change. [Energy Compacts][80] [More on Energy][81]
Sustainable Transport
While there is no single dedicated Sustainable Development Goal for transport, it is reflected in
several SDG targets and recognized as an enabler for achieving many of the goals. The United Nations
Decade of Sustainable Transport will be an opportunity to further raise awareness of transport’s
crucial role in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals and to gather and rally new solutions,
resources and partnerships to advance sustainable transport globally. [UN Decade of Sustainable
Transport 2026 – 2035][82] [More on Sustainable Transport][83]
Water
Water is fundamental to sustainable development, underpinning health, food security, energy,
ecosystems, and economic growth. Ensuring universal access to safe drinking water and sanitation,
improving water quality, strengthening water management, and enhancing resilience to water-related
risks are essential for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and addressing climate change
impacts. The 2026 UN Water Conference will take place from 2–4 December 2026 in the United Arab
Emirates. Co-hosted by Senegal and the United Arab Emirates, the Conference aims to accelerate the
implementation of SDG 6 on clean water and sanitation, strengthen global water governance, and
further elevate water-related issues on the international agenda through concrete action and
partnerships. [2026 UN Water Conference][84] [More on Water and Sanitation][85]
Oceans
SDG 14: Life Below Water aims to conserve and sustainably use the world's oceans, seas, and marine
resources by 2030. Key targets include reducing marine pollution, protecting ecosystems, ending
overfishing, and minimizing ocean acidification. It is critical for managing climate change,
biodiversity, and coastal livelihoods. The high-level 2025 United Nations Conference to Support the
Implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 14: Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and
marine resources for sustainable development (the 2025 UN Ocean Conference) was co-hosted by France
and Costa Rica and held in Nice, France, from 9 – 13 June 2025. [2025 UN Ocean Conference][86]
[UNOC3 Political Declaration][87] [More on Oceans & Seas][88]
Small Island Developing States
Small Island Developing States (SIDS) face unique and interrelated challenges, including climate
change impacts, ocean degradation, limited resources, and structural vulnerabilities, while also
demonstrating leadership and innovation in advancing sustainable development. Strengthening
partnerships, mobilizing finance, and enhancing capacity-building are essential to support SIDS in
achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and ensuring that no one is left behind. The Fourth
International Conference on Small Island Developing States marked a key milestone in advancing SIDS
priorities and resulted in the adoption of the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS, which provides a
renewed framework for action, partnerships, and implementation. [4th Conference on SIDS][89]
[ABAS][90] [SIDS Partnership Framework][91] [More on SIDS][92]
Stakeholder Engagement
Stakeholder engagement is central to advancing the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. The
High-level Political Forum on Sustainable Development (HLPF) serves as the United Nations’ main
platform for inclusive dialogue, bringing together governments, civil society, the private sector,
academia, and other stakeholders to share experiences, build partnerships, and strengthen
implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals. [More information][93] [Subscribe to mailing
list][94]
Partnerships for the SDGs
Partnerships are critical for accelerating progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals by
bringing together governments, civil society, the private sector, academia, and the UN system.
Effective multi-stakeholder partnerships help mobilize resources, scale innovative solutions, and
strengthen implementation across sectors and levels. The 2026 ECOSOC Partnership Forum took place on
27 January 2026 at the UN Headquarters in New York under the theme “Transformative, equitable,
innovative and coordinated actions for the 2030 Agenda and its SDGs for a sustainable future for
all”. [2026 ECOSOC Partnership Forum][95] [SDG Actions Platform][96] [Partnership Accelerator][97]
[SDG Acceleration Actions][98] [More on Partnerships][99]
Capacity Development
Capacity development is essential for advancing sustainable development, enabling governments and
stakeholders to strengthen skills, institutions, data systems, and partnerships needed to design,
implement, and monitor integrated solutions across the economic, social, and environmental
dimensions of the 2030 Agenda. The Division’s capacity development activities advance the
implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the ABAS and other internationally
agreed development goals, guided by the outcomes of United Nations intergovernmental bodies on the
three pillars of sustainable development – social, economic and environmental. [Micro-, Small and
Medium-sized Enterprises (MSMEs)][100] [UN-Portugal Ocean Fellowship][101] [Partnership
Accelerator][102] [More on Capacity Development][103]
Higher Education for Sustainable Development
Higher education plays a critical role in advancing sustainable development by generating knowledge,
educating future leaders, fostering innovation, supporting evidence-informed policymaking, and
working with communities, governments, civil society, business and the UN system to translate ideas
into action. UN DESA supports the Higher Education Sustainability Initiative (HESI) as a platform
that mobilizes higher education institutions, networks, students and partners to advance sustainable
development. [Higher Education Sustainability Initiative][104] [2026 HESI Global Forum][105]
[SDG Actions Platform] [Visit the SDG Actions Platform][106]
SDG Registries & Databases
Over the years, UN DESA has developed and maintained a range of SDG registries and databases that
capture commitments, partnerships, and actions by governments, the United Nations system, and a wide
range of stakeholders. These platforms support transparency, accountability, and knowledge-sharing,
and help track progress and implementation across the 2030 Agenda. Together, these registries bring
together thousands of entries originating from major UN conferences, intergovernmental processes,
and country-led efforts. They provide publicly accessible information on voluntary commitments,
